first_message: Requests are failing across an entire region. It is our cloud object store, and products relying on it are having trouble too. We cannot read, enumerate, write or erase objects through the APIs. Virtual machine provisioning, disk volumes that fetch snapshot contents from the object store, on-demand function execution and the storage control panel are having trouble. Our status page controls will not let us post product-specific notices either.

first_message: People are reporting failed connections. We run a live messaging application. Certain chat communities look disconnected, their hosting workers are acting strangely, and people are struggling to join. Now certain chat communities look disconnected, one hosting worker is unhealthy, and several workers maintaining client sessions are acting strangely.

first_message: Updates are taking much longer than usual. The shared cluster that lets our applications locate one another is in poor health. Credential delivery is sluggish too, and numerous backend applications rely on that infrastructure. Typical key-value updates are taking a couple of seconds rather than a fraction of one, and a single host has elevated processor utilization. Members are falling behind on updates, the primary keeps losing synchronization with voting peers, and downstream applications are failing health assessments.

Scaling out its Kubernetes workloads brought API success rates close to normal, yet the console remains unreliable and backend failures persist.

first_message: We suddenly have a surge of authorization failures. The errors are coming from our worldwide key-based data store. Web publishing, identity checks and releases of edge workloads are among the products relying on it. Storage reads, writes, removals and key enumeration are rejected as unauthorized. Hosted static websites throw server-side errors, sign-in is unreliable, publishing edge programs fails and other dependent features are down. Identity failures are also keeping us from using our regular release reversal tools.

first_message: Groups of servers are dropping together. Our advertising gateway is down: it accepts requests, handles competitive bidding and delivers the selected creative. All traffic entering our advertising platform goes through it. Groups of machines are going down, requests go unhandled, bidding rounds fail to finish and selected ads never get delivered. Pages using direct requests may render incorrectly, and we cannot bid through third-party exchanges.

first_message: People can't open their code projects. It's our online workspace for software teams, running on Postgres with a main instance paired with a live replica. Earlier, lots of customers couldn't submit discussion replies on tickets or proposed code changes; now the platform is down. Our replica lagged until synchronization ceased because the transaction logs it needed were no longer on the main server. Fresh database copying attempts seemed to stall, one reported a shortage of replication slots, and after a configuration change the database initially failed to start due to excessive semaphore allocation.

first_message: Media playback keeps breaking. The backend that supplies details about shows and short segments is struggling, while a group of common cache hosts has independently gone offline. Our media clients and various web features depend on these systems. The database is under intense pressure and numerous calls for media descriptions are unsuccessful at the application tier. A group of cache hosts is down too, cutting off several offerings such as our landing page and online streaming service. Clients retaining their own copies of media descriptions can deliver limited material, whereas those fetching it straight from the backend are breaking.
